title: Help scenarios and help card
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y7 lesson 9 (Help scenarios and help card (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 9: Asking for help; trusted adults. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: When to ask for help
points: A worry that will not go away
Feeling unsafe at home, school or online

panels.title: Who can help
points: TGA: form tutor, any teacher, designated safeguarding lead

panels.title: How to ask
points: Say: 'Can I talk to you about something?'
Message the teacher privately in Teams if speaking is hard

panels.title: Safeguarding and confidentiality
points: If someone is at risk, adults must pass it on
That is to keep you safe, not to get you in trouble

blocks.h: Five situations: get help, and who?

questions.q: Someone in an online game keeps asking for your home address.
questions.a: Get help now: block, report and tell a parent and the TGA safeguarding lead.

questions.q: You feel low most days and have stopped enjoying things for several weeks.
questions.a: Get help: talk to a parent, your form tutor or the safeguarding lead; a GP can help too.

questions.q: You find a maths topic hard and are falling behind.
questions.a: Ask for help: your maths teacher, in the lesson chat or after the lesson.

questions.q: A friend tells you they are being hurt at home and asks you to keep it secret.
questions.a: Get help: you cannot keep this secret; tell the TGA safeguarding lead or a trusted adult straight away.

questions.q: You had an argument with a sibling and it is now sorted.
questions.a: You may not need help: it is sorted. Talk to a parent if it keeps happening.

keywords.def: a grown-up who listens and keeps you safe
the staff member responsible for keeping pupils safe
kept private, unless someone is at risk of harm

questions.q: Who could you tell at TGA if something worried you?
questions.a: My form tutor, any teacher or the safeguarding lead.

questions.q: Core: Scenarios sheet (pupil PDF): for five situations, decide whether to get help and who.
questions.a: Help sought from an appropriate adult for each risky situation.

questions.q: Extend: Make a personal help card: three people at home, two at TGA, one helpline.
Stretch: In the portal response box, explain why a teacher cannot always keep a secret. Start: 'A teacher must pass on...'
questions.a: A teacher must pass on a worry when a child may be at risk, so the right people can keep them safe.

questions.q: A friend messages that someone online is asking for their photos. What should you do?
options: Tell a trusted adult straight away
questions.a: B) Tell a trusted adult straight away. This is a safeguarding risk; adults can act quickly to protect your friend.

questions.q: Childline's number is... A) 999 B) 0800 1111 C) 101
Big question: why do people keep problems to themselves, and what would you say to them?
questions.a: Fear or embarrassment; it is brave to tell, and adults can help.
